edges.effect_quant: The direct synthesis suggests passive post-exercise heat exposure can modestly improve endurance performance, though the evidence base is still small and protocol-sensitive.
edges.mechanism: Repeated heat exposure after training can expand plasma volume, strengthen thermoregulatory adaptation, and increase heat tolerance without adding much mechanical load. Those adaptations can translate into small endurance gains when the protocol is applied consistently.
edges.summary: The clearest evidence comes from the recent meta-analysis showing that passive post-exercise heat exposure improved endurance-performance outcomes on average. A broader review of recovery and training adaptations points in the same direction, and controlled heat-acclimation trials help explain why the effect is plausible rather than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: The literature is still relatively small, and protocols differ widely in temperature, immersion method, delay after exercise, and training status. This should be treated as a niche performance tool with emerging support, not as a universal endurance intervention.
